lesson.intro: El present perfect une el pasado con el presente. Se parece al 'he comido' español, pero sus reglas no son iguales: lo que decide es si mencionas un momento terminado del pasado.
when: Experiencias en tu vida, sin decir cuándo (I've been to London twice. Have you ever tried sushi?).
Algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora, con for o since (She has lived here since 2019).
Resultados recientes que importan ahora, a menudo con just, already o yet (I've lost my keys. Have you finished yet?).
Si dices CUÁNDO pasó con un tiempo terminado (yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago), usa pasado simple: I saw him yesterday.
For + duración (for two years, for a week). Since + punto de inicio (since 2019, since Monday, since I was a child).

form.label: Estructura
items: I've finished / She's finished / They've finished
Negativa: I haven't finished / He hasn't finished
Pregunta: Have you finished? / Has she finished?

form.label: Participios irregulares frecuentes
items: be → been, go → gone, see → seen, do → done
eat → eaten, write → written, take → taken
know → known, lose → lost, fly → flown

form.label: Posición de las palabras
items: just, already, never, ever: entre have y el participio (I've just eaten)
yet: al final, en preguntas y negativas (I haven't finished yet)

examples.en: We've known each other for ten years.
examples.es: Nos conocemos desde hace diez años.

errors.why: 'Yesterday' es un tiempo terminado: pasado simple.
En español usamos presente ('vivo aquí desde'), pero en inglés va present perfect.

errors.wrong: I know her since three years.
errors.right: I have known her for three years.
errors.why: Duración = for. Y el verbo va en present perfect.

errors.wrong: Have you finished already your homework?
errors.right: Have you finished your homework yet?
errors.why: En preguntas se usa 'yet' al final de la frase.

lesson.tip: Si en la frase aparece un momento terminado (yesterday, ago, last…, in + año pasado), olvídate del present perfect.

checks.explain: 'Last week' es un tiempo terminado: pasado simple.
2021 es el punto de inicio: since.
Experiencia con 'ever' y participio 'been': Have you ever been…?

practice.explain: 'In 2019' es un momento terminado: pasado simple.
Empezó en el pasado y sigue: present perfect (simple o continuo).

practice.prompt: I can't find my keys. I think I ___ (lose) them.
practice.explain: Resultado que importa ahora (no encuentro las llaves): have lost.

practice.prompt: I have known her ___ ten years.

practice.explain: 2015 es el punto de inicio: since.

answers: I have been living here since 2020.
practice.explain: 'Desde 2020' y sigue: present perfect, no presente simple.

answers: I have never been to London.
practice.explain: 'Never' va entre have y el participio.

answers: Have you finished your homework yet?
Have you finished the homework yet?
Have you already finished your homework?
Have you finished your homework already?
practice.explain: En preguntas, 'ya' suele ser 'yet' al final. 'Already' en pregunta muestra sorpresa.
'Just' va entre has y el participio: has just called.

challenge.sentence: I started working here three years ago.
challenge.explain: 'Hace tres años y sigo' = present perfect + for.

challenge.sentence: This is the first time I have eaten Thai food.
challenge.explain: 'Es la primera vez' equivale a 'nunca antes': have never eaten.

challenge.sentence: The last time I saw Laura was in May.
challenge.explain: 'La última vez fue en mayo' = no la he visto desde mayo.

challenge.sentence: How long are you living in this town?
answers: How long have you lived in this town?
How long have you been living in this town?
challenge.explain: 'How long' sobre algo que sigue: present perfect.
